question.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨{y}^{2}+8x{y}^{3},\,{e}^{x}+2{y}^{2}⟩
$$

through the boundary of the square $-1\le x\le 0,0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129319/assets/bb0033d2b275442ee92cc0b805c71102641c670ea1b0edba97d31a9262795c83.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={y}^{2}+8x{y}^{3}$ and $Q(x,y)={e}^{x}+2{y}^{2}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=8{y}^{3},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =4y.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 0,\,0\le y\le 1\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(8{y}^{3}+4y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{0}(8{y}^{3}+4y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(8{y}^{3}+4y)\,x\,{|}_{-1}^{0}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(8{y}^{3}+4y)\cdot 1\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(8{y}^{3}+4y)\,dy \\  & =[2{y}^{4}+2{y}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(2(1)^{4}+2(1)^{2})-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
